claim: The note explains も by what it replaces, naming が (ga), a particle no card has taught.
evidence: Note: 'Replaces は (wa) or が (ga) on the noun it marks (not added alongside them)'. が appears on no card in the ledger or in this chapter.
fix: Explain も against は and を, which I have met (juice-mo-onegaishimasu already does this for を), and leave が until it is taught.
verdictReason: Both roles, same claim; merged. The ledger before this unit (439 cards) teaches は, の, か, から, まで and を (inside おねがいします sentences) and never が; the collection's first が card is in chapter-6. The book's GRAMMAR 2 says only that も means too/also/either and is always used with a noun. Drop 'or が (ga)'; は and を (which juice-mo-onegaishimasu's note already uses) carry the point.

claim: 'I would like ..., please' is the deck's English for おねがいします everywhere else, so on this front I answer これをおねがいします and am marked wrong.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'I would like this one, please.' Answer: これをください. Compare chapter-4/ks4-curry-salad 'I would like curry and salad, please.' = カレーとサラダをおねがいします and chapter-4-extras/kohi-o-onegaishimasu 'I would like a coffee, please.' = コーヒーをおねがいします, while the other ください cards say 'I'll take ...' or 'X, please.'
fix: Gloss it the way the other ください cards are glossed, e.g. 'I'll take this one, please.', or add the kohi-o-kudasai hint.
verdictReason: Checked every ください and おねがいします card in both units. 'I would like …, please' is the English of all six おねがいします sentences (ks4-curry-salad, kohi-o-onegaishimasu, sumimasen-sandoitchi-to-kohi, to-koucha-choko-keki, sarada-mo-onegaishimasu, juice-mo-onegaishimasu) and of exactly one ください sentence, this one; the other seven ください cards say 'I'll take …' or 'X, please.' The English is the book's own KS3 gloss, so the book is not at fault, but card-rules-shared says that when one English shape maps to two structures the hint names the structure, and これをおねがいします is a sentence the learner can build from Lesson 1 and 2 cards. A hint in the kohi-o-kudasai style keeps the book's English; reglossing to 'I'll take this one, please.' also works.

claim: The English fits both をください and をおねがいします, which this chapter teaches as two ways to order, and nothing on the front picks one.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Food / I would like curry and salad, please.' Answer: カレーとサラダをおねがいします. The ください card says 'noun を (o) ください (kudasai) used when shopping or ordering'. Only the kohi-o-kudasai / kohi-o-onegaishimasu pair carries a hint telling the two apart.
fix: Give it the same hint kohi-o-onegaishimasu uses ('the wider-use polite request ...').
verdictReason: True as stated: the front fits both をください and をおねがいします and no cue picks one; only the kohi pair carries hints. Left at polish rather than raised, because once ks3 is fixed the deck's English is consistent ('I would like' = おねがいします, 'I'll take' / 'X, please' = ください) and the unit-level finding on chapter-4-extras covers how to make that convention visible once. If the fixer adds hints instead, this card gets the kohi-o-onegaishimasu one.

claim: The hint on the Recognition front says what と means, so the card no longer asks me anything.
evidence: Recognition FRONT: 'と / joining two nouns into a list'. Answer: 'And (particle)'. At this point と has only one use I know, so the hint has nothing to tell apart.
fix: Show the hint on the Production front only, or hold it back until a second use of と is taught.
verdictReason: The line on the Recognition front is a `scene` (cards.json: scene 'joining two nouns into a list'), not a hint, and it is required: chapter-6 cards と again as 'With, together with (particle)' (to-particle-with, scene 'doing something together with someone'), so the two と cards share a target and the collision rule demands a scene on both faces of both. The authoring rules accept that for a grammar word 'a small leak is the accepted price of an answerable card'. The Learner cannot see chapter-6 yet, but the deck is studied shuffled as a whole.

claim: The hint on the Recognition front spells out the meaning the card asks for.
evidence: Recognition FRONT: 'で / paying, or doing something by a method'. Answer: 'By means of (particle)'. で has only this one use among the cards I have studied.
fix: Show the hint on the Production front only, or until a second で is taught.
verdictReason: Same as to-particle: the line is a `scene` ('paying, or doing something by a method'), and で is carded again as a particle in chapter-7 (de-particle-transport), chapter-8 (particle-de-place 'At, in, on', scene 'marking where the action happens'), chapter-19 and chapter-21. Four later cards share the target, so the scene is mandatory and its small leak is the accepted price.

claim: The note refers to 'the source', which a learner studying the deck does not have.
evidence: Note: 'Suffix — attaches directly after a number (written 〜えん (en) in the source), e.g. 3,000えん (en)'.
fix: Drop 'in the source' and keep the example.
verdictReason: Note reads exactly as quoted. 'In the source' is an authoring reference the learner has nothing to resolve. The book does write it 〜えん, so 'written 〜えん (en) after a number, e.g. 3,000えん' keeps the information without the reference.

claim: Several ordering cards have English that fits both をください and をおねがいします, and only one pair (kohi-o-kudasai / kohi-o-onegaishimasu) carries the hint that separates them.
evidence: orange-juice-o-kudasai 'An orange juice, please.' (ください); sumimasen-sandoitchi-to-kohi 'Excuse me. I would like a sandwich and coffee, please.', to-koucha-choko-keki 'I would like a black tea and a chocolate cake, please.', sarada-mo-onegaishimasu 'I would like a salad as well, please.', juice-mo-onegaishimasu 'I would like a juice as well, please.' (all おねがいします). None has a hint. kohi-o-kudasai has 'the blunter of the two requests ...' and kohi-o-onegaishimasu 'the wider-use polite request ...'.
fix: Either put the kohi-pair hints on every ordering card, or keep the English rule strict ('I'll take' / 'X, please' = ください, 'I would like' = おねがいします) and state it once in the ください note.
verdictReason: Checked all five named cards: none carries a hint or scene; only kohi-o-kudasai / kohi-o-onegaishimasu do. The ください cards follow one implicit English convention ('I'll take …' / 'X, please.') and the おねがいします cards another ('I would like …'), but nothing tells the learner so, and ks3-kore-kudasai in the base unit breaks it. The cheaper fix is the second option: fix ks3 and state the convention once, on the kudasai card's note or the kohi pair. (fib-pasokon-to-mausu-o-onegaishimasu and fib-mausu-o-kudasai are excluded and not in play.)

claim: The note talks about 'the スマホ distance set', an authoring grouping I never see in a shuffled deck.
evidence: Note: 'Closes the スマホ (sumaho) distance set with a negative, and shows the deny-then-correct move in full.'
fix: Keep the second half ('shows the deny-then-correct move') and drop the reference to a set.
verdictReason: Note reads exactly as quoted. 'The スマホ distance set' names an authoring group (kore-wa-sumaho-desu, ks1-sore-smartphone, this card) that a shuffled deck never shows together. Keep the deny-then-correct half.

claim: The note points to 'GRAMMAR 2', a section of a book the learner does not have open.
evidence: Note: '... も (mo) behaves identically in positive and negative sentences, which is the point GRAMMAR 2 makes.'
fix: End the note at 'sentences'.
verdictReason: Note reads exactly as quoted. 'GRAMMAR 2' is a section number of a book the learner does not have open ('from an earlier lesson' is the deck's accepted phrasing; a section number is not). The claim before it, that も behaves identically in positive and negative sentences, is the book's and stands alone.

claim: The note leans on 'GRAMMAR 4's rule', which the learner cannot look up.
evidence: Note: 'と (to) joins pronouns as readily as nouns — GRAMMAR 4's rule is about nouns generally, not just names of things.'
fix: Say it without the book reference, e.g. 'と joins これ and それ just as it joins names of things.'
verdictReason: Note reads exactly as quoted. The content is sound (GRAMMAR 4 says と connects nouns; これ/それ are pronouns, so the extension is fair), but the section reference is unusable from a card. Say it without the reference, as the Learner suggests.

claim: The note's only content is a pointer to 'GRAMMAR 2', which the learner cannot see.
evidence: Note: 'The affirmative of これはわたしのかさじゃありません (kore wa watashi no kasa ja arimasen), the sentence GRAMMAR 2 builds its も (mo) example on.'
fix: Keep 'The affirmative of これはわたしのかさじゃありません' and drop the book reference.
verdictReason: Note reads exactly as quoted. Checked the chapter: GRAMMAR 2 does build its も example on これはわたしのかさじゃありません, so the reference is accurate, but it points at the book rather than at the deck. mo-example-umbrella in the base unit carries that very sentence, so 'the affirmative of これはわたしのかさじゃありません' is a complete note on its own.

claim: The romaji writes いいえ as 'iie', where every other card spells it 'īe'.
evidence: Says: 'iie, rimokon desu'. Compare chapter-4/fib-c4-mechanical-pencil-a 'īe, shāpen desu.' and chapter-4-extras/iie-taburetto-desu 'īe, taburetto desu.'
fix: Write it 'īe, rimokon desu.'
verdictReason: The inconsistency inside this chapter is real (fib-c4-mechanical-pencil-a and iie-taburetto-desu write 'īe'), but 'every other card' is not: across the collection 33 pronunciations write 'īe' and 28 write 'iie' (chapter-1-extras, 3-extras, 6, 6-extras, 7-extras, 9-extras, 10, 10-extras, 11, 11-extras, 13, 13-extras, 23-extras). And src/translate/romajiStyle.js's long-vowel-exceptions rule says 'いい stays ii', which favours this card's spelling over the 33. What settles it: the owner picks one spelling for いいえ and the fixer sweeps the whole collection; a one-card edit in either direction fixes nothing.

claim: 'Watch' is also the whole gloss of うでどけい, which I learned in Lesson 2, so the front fits two answers.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'Shopping / Please show me the watch.' Answer: とけいをみせてください. chapter-2 'とけい | Watch, clock'; chapter-2-extras 'うでどけい | Watch'.
fix: Gloss とけい here as 'the clock' or 'the watch (とけい)', or add a hint that it is the general word.
verdictReason: Both words are taught: とけい 'Watch, clock' (chapter-2) and うでどけい 'Watch' (chapter-2-extras, card watch). But the うでどけい card carries hint 'the item you wear on your wrist, not the general word for a clock' and a note naming とけい as 'the broader word for any watch or clock', so the learner has been told which is the general word, and a bare 'the watch' leans toward it. Whether a sentence whose noun has a taught near-synonym counts as a collision is a judgement the collision rule (which keys on a shared gloss or target) does not settle. If the owner says it does, 'Please show me the clock.' or a one-word hint is the fix.

claim: Same collision: 'a watch' could be とけい or うでどけい, both of which I have been taught as 'watch'.
evidence: Production FRONT: 'This is a watch. That one is a watch too.' Answer: これはとけいです。それもとけいです. chapter-2-extras 'うでどけい | Watch'.
fix: Use 'clock' in the English, or add a hint naming the general word.
verdictReason: Same question as tokei-o-misete-kudasai, same answer: うでどけい is cued as the wristwatch specifically and とけい is named as the general word, so the collision is softer than the claim says, and whether it counts is the owner's call. 'This is a clock. That one is a clock too.' is the cheap fix if it does.

claim: The note says ください cannot ask for a service, but みせてください, おしえてください and ちょっとまってください all use it to ask someone to do something.
evidence: Note: 'ください (kudasai) literally asks for something to be given to you, so it fits a drink or a purchase but cannot ask for a service.' Compare chapter-4/misete-kudasai 'Please show me' and chapter-0 'ちょっとまってください | Wait just a moment, please.'
fix: Narrow it to the pattern on the card: 'noun をください asks for a thing; for a service use おねがいします'.
verdictReason: Note reads exactly as quoted. The learner has met ちょっとまってください (chapter-0), おしえてください (chapter-2-extras) and みせてください (this unit), all ください asking for an action, so 'ください … cannot ask for a service' contradicts three cards the learner knows. The book's GRAMMAR 3 limits the contrast to the noun を ください pattern. Narrow the note to that pattern, as the Learner's fix says.

evidence: Book, WORD POWER PLUS ONE chart (image Page_031_Image_0001): '100,000 じゅうまん'. Deck carries num-10000 いちまん, num-100million いちおく, num-1billion じゅうおく, num-10billion ひゃくおく, num-100billion せんおく and num-1trillion いっちょう, but nothing for じゅうまん in either unit or the corpus.
fix: Add a number card じゅうまん (jūman) = 100,000 beside the other PLUS ONE rows.
verdictReason: Checked the PLUS ONE chart image (Page_031_Image_0001): rows 1,000 せん, 10,000 いちまん, 100,000 じゅうまん, 1,000,000 ひゃくまん, 10,000,000 せんまん, 100,000,000 いちおく, … 1,000,000,000,000 いっちょう. Grepped every field of every cards.json in the collection: じゅうまん appears nowhere, and no exclusion names it. The deck cards six of the chart's nine rows above せん; the paradigm rule ('every cell of a paradigm the source lays out earns its own card') covers the chart, and the three missing rows are the ones a shopper is likeliest to need.

claim: The PLUS ONE chart's 1,000,000 row (ひゃくまん, one million) has no card, though the rarer rows above it are carded.
evidence: Book, PLUS ONE chart: '1,000,000 ひゃくまん'. No card in chapter-4 or chapter-4-extras targets ひゃくまん; the deck does card せんおく (100 billion) and いっちょう (1 trillion) from the same chart.
fix: Add a number card ひゃくまん (hyakuman) = 1,000,000 (one million).
verdictReason: Same chart, same check: ひゃくまん is on the chart's 1,000,000 row and in no card or exclusion anywhere in the collection. Card it beside じゅうまん and せんまん, in the base unit with the other PLUS ONE rows.

claim: The PLUS ONE chart's 10,000,000 row (せんまん) has no card.
evidence: Book, PLUS ONE chart: '10,000,000 せんまん'. No card in either unit targets せんまん; the chart's other rows from いちおく up are carded.

claim: The card's note sets this じゃ apart from the では contraction, while the book pairs じゃ with では as the same 'well then', and では itself is never carded.
evidence: Card ja: Production front 'Well then / the casual contraction'; note 'This じゃ (ja, 'well then') is a filler word marking a conclusion — not the same じゃ in じゃありません (ja arimasen) from an earlier lesson, which is a contraction of では (dewa) plus the negative; same sound, different job.' Book NOTES: 'じゃ and では correspond to "well" or "well then," interjections that express conclusion or resignation.' No card before this unit teaches では; chapter-6 carries dewa 'Well then' with hint 'the fuller, more formal form'.
fix: Rewrite the note to say じゃ is the casual form of では (dewa), both meaning 'well then' here, and only then contrast its job with the じゃ of じゃありません; make the hint name では.
verdictReason: Both roles saw the same contradiction; merged. Checked the faces: the hint says contraction, the note says this じゃ is a filler word and that the contraction of では is the other じゃ. The book pairs じゃ and では as one 'well then', and the deck's own chapter-6 dewa card ('the fuller, more formal form') treats this じゃ as the casual form of では, so the note's framing is the wrong half. The hint is right and must STAY: chapter-6's dewa shares the English 'Well then', a collection-wide gloss collision that needs a hint on both cards, so the Learner's 'drop the hint' option is out. Fix the note as the Reader says: this じゃ is the casual form of では, both 'well then' (では itself arrives in Lesson 6); then contrast its job with the じゃ of じゃありません.

claim: The hint calls ください 'the blunter of the two requests', a register claim the book does not make; the book separates ください and おねがいします by scope only.
evidence: Book GRAMMAR 3: '"noun を ください" means "please give me," and can be used when shopping or placing an order... "noun を おねがいします" can be used not only for making purchases... but for asking someone to do something or for requesting a service.' Card hint: 'the blunter of the two requests, the one that asks for the thing itself'. Its twin kohi-o-onegaishimasu says in its note 'Same order, softer and broader.'
fix: Change the hint to the book's distinction, e.g. 'the one that only asks for a thing', and drop 'softer' from kohi-o-onegaishimasu's note.
verdictReason: The book's GRAMMAR 3 separates the two by what each can ask for (a thing to be given, versus also an action or a service) and never by register. 'Blunter' (this hint) and 'softer' (kohi-o-onegaishimasu's note) are the author's own, conventional but not the book's, and nothing the learner holds can check them. The hint is doing a real job (this pair is the deck's one explicit ください / おねがいします contrast), so replace rather than delete: keep 'the one that asks for the thing itself' and drop the register words on both cards.

claim: The note romanises ちょう as 'chou', where the deck's romaji style writes the long vowel with a macron.
evidence: Card note: 'ちょう (chou) is the counting unit for one trillion'. The same card's romaji is 'itchō'.
fix: Write 'ちょう (chō)'.
verdictReason: Note reads 'ちょう (chou)'; the card's own pronunciation is 'itchō' and romajiStyle's long-vowel-macron rule forbids 'ou'. Preflight's note-romaji check compares only against strings the deck has a card for, and ちょう has none, so it did not catch this.

evidence: Book: 'シャーペン mechanical pencil (colloquial shortening of シャープペンシル)'. Card note: 'Colloquial shortening of シャープペンシル (shaapupenshiru)'; the card's own romaji is 'shāpen'.

verdictReason: Note reads 'シャープペンシル (shaapupenshiru)'; the card's own pronunciation is 'shāpen' and the deck's style writes long vowels with macrons. Not caught by preflight for the same reason as num-1trillion (no card for the quoted string).
